title: Applying a frozen rule to the proxy instead of the truth: mislabel mass under a margin condition and an exact Loewner sandwich on the retained information
statement: Frozen rule q on score space, Z = q(s), Z_hat = q(s_hat), s_hat = s + e, both retained informations computed from the true s; M = {Z != Z_hat}, pi = P(M). (i) If q(s_hat) != q(s) then dist(s, boundary of the cell of q(s)) <= ||e|| in any norm (the segment [s, s_hat] is connected); for a nearest-centre rule with positive-definite metric G, distinct centres and distance measured in G the squared distance is min_{b' != b} (||s - mu_b'||_G^2 - ||s - mu_b||_G^2)^2 / (4 ||mu_b - mu_b'||_G^2), rational on rational data. Hence with the margin function M_q(t) = P(dist_V(s, boundary q) <= t) and eps^2 = E[e^T V^{-1} e]: pi <= inf_t {M_q(t) + eps^2 / t^2}; if M_q(t) <= C t^alpha then pi <= (1 + alpha/2)(2/alpha)^(alpha/(alpha+2)) C^(2/(alpha+2)) eps^(2 alpha/(alpha+2)), i.e. pi <= 1.89 C^(2/3) eps^(2/3) at alpha = 1. (ii) With c_b the Z-cell means and c_hat_b the Z_hat-cell means of s: I_Zhat >= I_Z - Gamma and I_Z >= I_Zhat - Gamma_hat in the Loewner order, Gamma = 2 E[(s s^T + c_{Z_hat} c_{Z_hat}^T) 1_M], Gamma_hat = 2 E[(s s^T + c_hat_Z c_hat_Z^T) 1_M]. Corollaries: |tr R_Z - tr R_Zhat| <= 2 E[||w||^2 1_M] + 2 pi max_b max(||c'_b||^2, ||c_hat'_b||^2) (whitened); log eta_D(Z_hat) - log eta_D(Z) >= log(1 - gamma_R) with gamma_R = tr(I_Z^{-1} Gamma) <= tr(V^{-1} Gamma)/rho_min and tr(V^{-1} Gamma) = 2 E[(||w||^2 + ||c'_{Z_hat}||^2) 1_M], symmetrically above; order O(pi) for uniformly bounded whitened scores; O(sqrt pi) under a uniform fourth moment and stable positive base-cell masses as specified in the assumptions. Determinant rates also require a retained eigenvalue floor. Composed with (i) at alpha = 1: O(eps^(2/3)) bounded, O(eps^(1/3)) with a fourth moment. Without a margin condition nothing holds: CE-SCORE-ERROR-BOUNDARY-ATOM-001 has an atom of mass 1/2 on a cell boundary, pi = 1/2 for every eps > 0 and the retention jumps 4/5 -> 1/2.
assumptions: One law on x-space with finite second moments; fixed measurable cells with topological boundary distance in the same positive-definite norm used for the error. Distinct centres are required only for the Voronoi distance formula; ties follow a fixed convention.

The margin power law has C>0, alpha>0 and must hold at t*=(2 eps^2/(alpha C))^(1/(alpha+2)); otherwise optimize only over its valid range. Cap probability bounds by one. Zero error gives no disagreement. The exponent 2 alpha/(alpha+2) is for the L2 norm, not its square.

Both label maps take values in the same finite alphabet. A conditional centroid of a zero-mass cell is set to zero, including when reused by the other labeling; the Loewner inequalities need only finite second moments.

The determinant comparison requires I_Z positive definite and gamma_R<1; a reverse finite logarithmic comparison requires the corresponding proxy-label matrix and budget. The trace comparison needs no retained-rank condition.

Asymptotic O(sqrt pi) transfer: fixed law, finite base partition with minimum positive occupied mass p*>0, finite fourth whitened moment, pi->0. On original occupied cells p_hat>=p*/2 eventually, bounding their new centroids; original empty cells are null in the reverse cross-centroid term. Uniform statements over changing laws/rules require uniform fourth moments and p*. Determinant rates additionally require a uniform retained eigenvalue floor.
Measured quadrature values and finite exact searches are evidence only. This is a deterministic rule-transfer inequality, not a refitted-rule CLT or an excess Bayes-risk theorem.

proof_location.section: O8. Score-error budget for a frozen rule: what an estimated score costs, to first order

role: the boundary-displacement half of OP17: the loss of deploying a frozen rule on the proxy instead of the truth; with SCORE-ERROR-RETENTION-BUDGET it composes into the deployed-versus-oracle budget of O8.6
warning: Audited after explicit metric, empty-cell, margin-range and rate assumptions. The Markov/margin argument is published comparison machinery; the Loewner sandwich is the project reduction. The bound is often vacuous at measured door3 error scales.
